method: matched observed-patch design: within comets seen from the same geocentric sky region at perihelion epoch, a sky-localized systematic predicts the discrepancy tracks observed direction, while a boundary at the declared axis predicts it tracks aphelion direction.

matched_patch_radii.note: same observed sky patch: a zonal systematic acts on patch members irrespective of aphelion direction; a boundary predicts the in-cap members remain discrepant and the out-of-cap members do not

patch_theta_vs_d.note: within the observed patch: systematic predicts ~0; boundary predicts d_of growing toward the axis (negative rho)

incap_geosep_vs_d.note: does the observed position within the affected region modulate the anomaly? a patch systematic requires it; measured flat

outcap_theta_vs_d.note: does the aphelion-direction gradient continue beyond the cap edge? a sharp boundary predicts a continuous slope, not a step

partial_spearman.note: rank-residualized partial Spearman; the surviving partial correlation identifies which direction the anomaly tracks

geometry_channels.note: solar elongation at perihelion epoch and galactic latitude of the observed direction -- the two classic crowding/twilight systematic channels
